note: The main banks: AIB and Bank of Ireland, Ireland's two largest retail banks; PTSB, the third, refused an automated request (403) and isn't written. AIB's credit card rates (last reviewed 14 April 2025, still the page AIB publishes) and its credit cards page (read 2026-10-30): the CLICK Visa (9.11% a year), Platinum Visa (11.84%), 'be' Visa and Student Visa (14.85%; for third-level students, not checked). The 'be' Visa's rate is 14.16% a year when 5,000 euros or more is spent in 12 months, otherwise 16.79%: written as the range 14.16% to 16.79%. AIB charges no annual bank fee; the government's 30-euro annual stamp duty on each credit card account is written as each card's yearly fee. The Ascent Visa, on the rates page but not among the cards AIB offers, and the four cards AIB no longer opens aren't written. Bank of Ireland's credit cards page (read 2026-10-30): the Aer Credit Card (14% a year; 6.50 euros a month), Classic (16.12%), Platinum (13.79%; 76.18 euros a year), Affinity (14.57%) and Student (14.54%; for full-time students, with a limit of 600 to 1,000 euros, not written), each with the 30-euro stamp duty as a yearly fee. Neither bank's pages give a cash advance, foreign transaction, minimum payment, grace period or default fee for these cards (AIB's fees and charges page refused an automated request), so none is written; introductory offers aren't written.
